easy.def: A very young child.
examples: The baby is asleep.
A baby smiled at me.
The baby drinks milk.

more.def: A very young child, or the young of an animal.
examples: The baby giggled when I made a silly face.
A baby elephant stays close to its mother.
My cousin just had a baby.

easy.def: To the place you left.
examples: I came back home.
Please give it back.
She went back to bed.

more.def: To a place or condition where someone or something was earlier.
examples: After the picnic, we walked back to the car.
He gave the library book back on Monday.
The tide goes out and then comes back in.

easy.def: The part of your body behind you, between your neck and your legs.
examples: My back hurts.
The cat has a soft back.
She carried me on her back.

more.def: The part of the body on the opposite side from the front, or the rear part of something.
examples: The turtle pulled its head into its shell on its back.
We sat in the back of the bus.
He scratched the dog's back with a brush.

easy.def: The part of a picture that is behind the main things.
examples: There are trees in the background.
The mountain is in the background.
The background is blue.

more.def: The part of a picture or scene that is behind the main thing.
examples: A tall mountain stood in the background of the photo.
The artist painted a blue sky in the background.
Soft music played in the background.

easy.def: With the back going first.
examples: He walked backwards.
I read the word backwards.
The car rolled backwards.

more.def: In the direction behind you, or in the opposite order.
examples: He walked backwards down the hall.
She said the alphabet backwards.
The truck rolled backwards down the hill.

easy.def: Not good.
examples: The milk smells bad.
That was a bad dream.
It is bad weather.

more.def: Not good, or causing harm or trouble.
examples: The bad weather kept us inside all weekend.
Eating too much candy is bad for your teeth.
He had a bad cold and stayed home from school.

easy.def: A small sign you wear to show who you are.
examples: The police officer wore a badge.
I got a badge for reading.
My badge says my name.

more.def: A small piece of metal, plastic or cloth that you wear or pin on to show who you are or what you did.
examples: The police officer wore a shiny badge.
She earned a badge for swimming.
My name badge was pinned to my shirt.

easy.def: In a bad way.
examples: I sang badly.
He played badly.
The old bike was badly rusted.

more.def: In a poor or unpleasant way, or very much.
examples: The team played badly and lost the game.
The old house needs a new roof badly.
The tomatoes were badly damaged by the frost.

easy.def: A soft holder for carrying things.
examples: Put your lunch in the bag.
My bag is heavy.
Mom has a bag of apples.

more.def: A container made of paper, plastic or cloth for carrying or holding things.
examples: She packed her swimsuit in a bag.
We filled three bags with leaves.
A bag of flour sat on the shelf.

easy.def: To throw water out of a boat.
examples: We bailed the boat.
She bailed water with a bucket.
Bail out the water.

more.def: To throw water out of a boat with a bucket or cup.
examples: We bailed water out of the little boat with a pail.
The sailors bailed all night to keep afloat.
She bailed the rain from the canoe.

easy.def: To stay up and not fall over.
examples: I can balance on one foot.
The seal balances a ball on its nose.
Can you balance a book on your head?

more.def: To keep yourself or an object steady so it does not tip or fall.
examples: The gymnast balanced on the narrow beam without wobbling.
He balanced the tray of drinks as he walked across the room.
It is hard to balance on a bike when you first learn to ride.

easy.def: A round toy.
examples: Throw the ball.
The dog chased the ball.
We kick the ball.

more.def: A round object used in games and sports.
examples: He threw the ball over the fence.
A basketball is a large orange ball.
The kitten batted a ball of yarn across the floor.

easy.def: A rubber bag that you fill with air.
examples: I blew up a balloon.
The balloon popped.
The balloon floated up.

more.def: A thin rubber bag that is filled with air or gas so that it gets big and round.
examples: I blew up a red balloon for the party.
The balloon floated up to the ceiling.
A hot air balloon rose over the field.

easy.def: A long, yellow fruit with a peel.
examples: I eat a banana.
The monkey ate a banana.
Peel the banana.

more.def: A long, curved fruit with a yellow skin that you peel before eating.
examples: I had a banana for a snack.
The monkey peeled the banana.
Bananas grow in bunches on tall plants.

easy.def: A group of people who play music.
examples: The band played.
I am in the school band.
The band played loud songs.

more.def: A group of musicians who play music together.
examples: The school band marched in the parade.
My cousin plays drums in a band.
The band played at the dance.

easy.def: A thin strip that holds things.
examples: Put a rubber band around the pencils.
She wore a band in her hair.
There is a band around the box.

more.def: A thin, flat strip of material that goes around something.
examples: She put a rubber band around the papers.
The gift had a red band around it.
A ring is a band of gold.

easy.def: A loud sudden sound.
examples: I heard a bang.
The door shut with a bang.
The bang scared the dog.

more.def: A loud, sudden noise like an explosion or a hit.
examples: We heard a loud bang in the garage.
The firecracker went off with a bang.
The bang of the drum made me jump.

easy.def: To hit hard and make noise.
examples: Do not bang the door.
He banged the drum.
She bangs on the table.

more.def: To hit something so that it makes a loud noise.
examples: The wind banged the door against the wall.
He banged the drum in time with the song.
She banged on the door to get our attention.

easy.def: A place that keeps money safe.
examples: Mom went to the bank.
I put money in the bank.
The bank closes at five.

more.def: A business that keeps people's money safe and lends money.
examples: She saved her allowance in the bank.
The bank is open from nine to five.
My parents went to the bank to talk about a loan.

easy.def: The land beside a river.
examples: We sat on the river bank.
Ducks walked along the bank.
The bank was muddy.

more.def: The sloping ground along the edge of a river or lake.
examples: We had a picnic on the bank of the river.
Frogs sat in the mud on the bank.
The boat was tied to the bank.

easy.def: A long, hard piece of something.
examples: A bar of soap.
He ate a granola bar.
A metal bar.

more.def: A long, straight piece of something hard.
examples: A metal bar held the gate shut.
She washed her hands with a bar of soap.
He ate a granola bar for a snack.

easy.def: Just; almost not.
examples: I barely made it.
He barely spoke.
She barely ate.

more.def: Only just; almost not at all.
examples: I barely made it to the bus on time.
The baby barely made a sound.
He could barely see in the dark.

easy.def: Something that costs little.
examples: The shoes were a bargain.
I got a bargain.
The bargain was good.

more.def: Something that costs less money than it normally would.
examples: The shoes were a bargain at half price.
She found a bargain at the yard sale.
This book is a bargain at two dollars.

easy.def: An agreement between two people.
examples: We made a bargain.
The bargain was fair.
A bargain is a deal.

more.def: An agreement in which each side promises something.
examples: We made a bargain that I would do the dishes if he took out the trash.
They kept their bargain.
The two friends made a bargain to share the toy.

easy.def: The tough outside covering of a tree.
examples: The bark is rough.
The squirrel climbed the bark.
I peeled the bark.

more.def: The rough covering on the trunk and branches of a tree.
examples: The rough bark of the oak tree scratched my hand.
Squirrels ran up the bark.
A bug hid under the loose bark.

easy.def: To make the loud sound that a dog makes.
examples: The dog barks.
The dog barked at the cat.
Do not bark.

more.def: To make a loud, sharp sound as a dog does.
examples: The dog barked at the mail carrier.
Seals can bark like dogs.
Our puppy barks when it wants to play.

easy.def: A big farm building for animals or hay.
examples: The cows are in the barn.
The barn is red.
Hay is in the barn.

more.def: A large farm building where animals, hay or machines are kept.
examples: The cows slept in the barn.
The farmer stored hay in the barn.
A red barn stood at the end of the lane.

easy.def: A large, round container for liquids.
examples: The barrel is full of water.
A barrel is made of wood.
The barrel rolled.

more.def: A large, round container with flat ends and curved sides, used to hold liquids.
examples: The barrel was filled with rainwater.
The old barrel was made of wood.
The workers rolled the barrel up the ramp.

easy.def: The bottom part of something.
examples: The base of the lamp is heavy.
We stood at the base of the tree.
The cup has a wide base.

more.def: The bottom part that something stands on.
examples: A wide base keeps the lamp from tipping.
The base of the statue is made of stone.
We camped at the base of the mountain.

easy.def: One of four places in baseball.
examples: Run to first base.
He slid to the base.
She stood on the base.

more.def: One of the four corners of a baseball field that a runner must touch.
examples: She slid into second base.
The bases are loaded.
He ran to first base.

easy.def: A game where you hit a ball with a bat and run around bases.
examples: I play baseball after school.
Baseball is a fun game.
We watched a baseball game.

more.def: A game played by two teams with a bat and a ball, where players run around four bases.
examples: Our baseball team practices twice a week.
The pitcher threw a fast baseball across the plate.
He hit a baseball over the fence for a home run.

easy.def: A room or floor below the ground in a house.
examples: The washing machine is in the basement.
We play in the basement.
The basement is cool.

more.def: A room or rooms in a building that are partly or fully below the ground.
examples: Dad stores the tools in the basement.
We play table tennis in the basement.
The basement stays cool even on hot days.

easy.def: Simple and most important.
examples: These are basic rules.
She learned basic math.
The basic idea is easy.

more.def: Forming the starting point of something, simple and necessary.
examples: We learned the basic rules of the game.
Reading is a basic skill.
The basic idea of the story is easy to follow.

easy.def: A container for carrying things.
examples: The fruit is in a basket.
I carry a basket.
The basket is full.

more.def: A container made of woven strips of wood, reeds or plastic, used for carrying things.
examples: She picked berries and put them in a basket.
A basket of apples sat on the table.
The cat slept in a basket.

related.def: As much as fits in a basket.

easy.def: A game where you throw a ball into a high basket.
examples: I play basketball.
We watched basketball.
Basketball is fun.

more.def: A game in which two teams try to throw a large ball through a hoop.
examples: We play basketball in the gym after school.
The basketball bounced off the rim.
He scored two points in the basketball game.

easy.def: A small animal that flies at night.
examples: A bat flew out of the cave.
Bats sleep in the day.
We saw a bat in the barn.

more.def: A small furry animal with wings that sleeps in the day and flies at night.
examples: The bat hung upside down from the roof of the cave.
A bat can eat hundreds of insects in one night.
Bats use sound to find their way in the dark.

easy.def: A stick you use to hit a ball.
examples: She hit the ball with her bat.
My bat is made of wood.
He left his bat at the park.

more.def: A wooden or metal stick used to hit the ball in games like baseball and cricket.
examples: He swung the bat and sent the ball over the fence.
The coach handed each player a helmet and a bat.
Her new bat is lighter than her old one.

easy.def: To hit something, like a ball.
examples: The cat likes to bat the toy.
It is my turn to bat.
The baby bats at the toy over her crib.

more.def: To hit at something with a bat or with your hand or paw.
examples: The kitten batted the string back and forth.
Our best hitter will bat first in the next game.
She batted the balloon up into the air.

easy.def: A wash in a tub of water.
examples: I take a bath.
The baby has a bath.
The bath is warm.

more.def: A wash in which you sit or lie in a tub of water.
examples: I take a bath every evening.
The baby splashed in her bath.
The dog needed a bath.

easy.def: A room with a toilet and a sink.
examples: I brush my teeth in the bathroom.
The bathroom is down the hall.
May I go to the bathroom?

more.def: A room in a home or building that has a sink, a toilet and often a bath or shower.
examples: The bathroom is at the end of the hall.
She washed her hands in the bathroom.
Our school has a bathroom on every floor.

easy.def: A small thing that gives power to a toy or machine.
examples: The flashlight needs a battery.
The battery is dead.
I put new batteries in the toy.

more.def: A small container that stores electric power for a toy, a flashlight or a car.
examples: The toy stopped moving because the battery was dead.
Dad put new batteries in the flashlight.
A phone battery needs to be charged often.

easy.def: A big fight between armies.
examples: The battle was long.
The soldiers fought in a battle.
We read about a battle.

more.def: A fight between armies or groups.
examples: The battle lasted for three days.
Soldiers rested after the battle.
We read about a famous battle in history class.

easy.def: A part of the sea that goes into the land.
examples: Boats floated in the bay.
We swam in the bay.
The bay is calm.

more.def: A wide part of the sea that curves into the land, like a large bend.
examples: Sailboats drifted across the quiet bay.
Many fishing boats stay in the bay when it storms.
We walked along the beach around the bay.
